Empirical Research Plan  
“Hoy No Circula” and Mexico-City Air Quality  

----------------------------------------------------------------  
1. Identification Strategy  
Chosen method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with an event-study extension.

Why DID?  
• The policy was introduced city-wide on a known date and stayed in force thereafter, so we have a clear pre/post break.  
• Daily pollution is observed repeatedly at the same monitoring stations, giving us panel data with rich fixed-effect structure.  
• Weather shocks and seasonal patterns can be flexibly controlled.  
• We can bolster the single-treated-unit setting by (i) using all stations as repeated cross-sections and (ii) building a synthetic control from other large Mexican metro areas in robustness checks.  

----------------------------------------------------------------  
2. Treatment and Control  

Treatment variable  
Treat_it = 1 for monitor i on day t if t ≥ 1 January 2008 (illustrative start date of the tightened “Hoy No Circula” rules) and 0 otherwise. The coefficient on Treat_it captures the average change in pollution attributable to the permanent restriction regime.

Control group / counterfactual  
• Within-city counterfactual: the same monitors in the pre-policy period (parallel-trend assumption).  
• External counterfactual for robustness: monitors in Puebla, Toluca, Querétaro, etc., which did not change their driving-restriction rules at that time (constructed as a synthetic control).

Treatment timing  
Single jump on the official implementation date (replace 1 Jan 2008 with the actual date in the data).

----------------------------------------------------------------  
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  

A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of the policy, post-2008 pollution at Mexico-City stations would have followed the same trend as before 2008 (conditional on weather & seasonality).  
Plausibility: Reasonable because no other large air-quality regulation was introduced exactly then; we will test using event-study leads.

A2. No simultaneous city-wide shocks: No other intervention coincided with the policy start that could independently move pollution.  
Plausibility: Needs verification (e.g., fuel reform dates, refinery closures). Will perform historical scan and add date dummies if necessary.

A3. Stable measurement technology: Monitoring equipment and siting remain unchanged over the sample.  
Plausibility: Metadata can be checked; drop stations with hardware changes.

A4. SUTVA: One monitor’s potential pollution outcome is unaffected by the policy status at another monitor (reasonable within-city aggregate air box).  

----------------------------------------------------------------  
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation  

T1. Non-parallel pre-trends.  
• Graphical inspection and formal placebo DID on pre-period subsamples.  
• Include cubic time trends interacted with station-clusters; allow for differential seasonality.

T2. Weather mis-measurement/omission.  
• Add high-frequency controls: temperature, humidity, wind speed, precipitation, thermal inversion dummies.  
• Interact weather with month fixed effects.

T3. Other coincident environmental policies (fuel sulfur limits, bus rapid-transit roll-outs).  
• Collect dates of those reforms, include policy-specific dummies, or drop weeks around them.  
• Conduct difference-in-difference-in-differences (triple-D) comparing hours outside the driving-ban window (nighttime) vs affected hours (daytime) using hourly data in robustness.

----------------------------------------------------------------  
5. R Code Outline  

```r
# 0. Packages -----------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)   # fast data
library(fixest)       # regressions with FEs
library(did)          # event-study utilities
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load data ----------------------------------------------------------
poll <- fread("mxcity_pollution.csv")      # station_id, date, ozone, pm25
weather <- fread("mxcity_weather.csv")     # station_id, date, temp, wind, rh

poll <- merge(poll, weather, by = c("station_id","date"))

# 2. Variable construction ---------------------------------------------
poll[, date        := as.IDate(date)]
policy_start        <- as.IDate("2008-01-01")   # replace with true date
poll[, post         := as.integer(date >= policy_start)]
poll[, year         := year(date)]
poll[, dow          := weekdays(date)]
poll[, month        := month(date)]
poll[, yday         := yday(date)]

# event-study relative time (in days)
poll[, rel_day := as.integer(date - policy_start)]

# 3. Main specification -------------------------------------------------
# y_it = alpha_i + gamma_t + beta*post + Weather + eps_it
fe_formula <- ozone ~ post + temp + wind + rh | station_id + yday
did_main   <- feols(fe_formula, data = poll, cluster = "station_id")

summary(did_main)

# 4. Event-study --------------------------------------------------------
es <- sunab(data = poll, time = "date", cohort = "post")  # cohort=1 for all post
es_reg <- feols(ozone ~ es() + temp + wind + rh | station_id + yday, 
                data = poll, cluster = "station_id")
iplot(es_reg)      # lead-lag plot

# 5. Robustness: placebo date ------------------------------------------
placebo_start <- as.IDate("2006-01-01")
poll[, placebo := as.integer(date >= placebo_start & date < policy_start)]
placebo_reg <- feols(ozone ~ placebo + temp + wind + rh | station_id + yday, 
                     data = poll[date < policy_start + 365], 
                     cluster = "station_id")
summary(placebo_reg)
```

Notes:  
• Repeat regressions for PM2.5.  
• Change clustering to two-way (station × date) if many stations; use vcov = cluster.  
• Synthetic-control robustness available via Synth package; omitted for brevity.

----------------------------------------------------------------  
6. Expected Results  

Direction: Negative—restricting driving lowers traffic-related pollutants.  
Magnitude (back-of-envelope): Prior studies suggest 3–6 ppb drop in peak ozone (≈ 5-10 %) and 4–8 µg/m³ decline in PM2.5 on restricted days relative to baseline.

----------------------------------------------------------------  
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)  

C1. No interference (SUTVA) ......................... 1  
C2. Correct treatment timing & definition ........... 1  
C3. Parallel pre-trends verified .................... 1 (after tests)  
C4. No major simultaneous shocks .................... 0.5 (needs vetting)  
C5. Stable composition / measurement ................ 1  

Total ≈ 4.5 / 5 – Identification judged strong, contingent on passing pre-trend and shock checks.
